data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's own countercondition defeats its central claim in the context of the stated problem. The problem asks which 'published testing principles' support the proposed property. SRC_002 cites the Single Responsibility Principle (SRP), which is an object-oriented design heuristic about class cohesion, not a published testing principle governing test design and oracles. The countercondition 'If the system legitimately allows non-monotonic reordering or replacement... monotonicity alone is insufficient' concedes the asserted property is incomplete. The problem premise is merely that new evidence arrives; it does not restrict the system to append-only/shrink-only transitions, so a monotonicity assertion can fail to hold the general correctness property the problem demands, leaving SRC_002 without a valid published testing principle and with an inadequate proposed property.
